summary: Commit 002c5a7 (src/logic/followUps.ts, tests/unit/followUps.test.ts, two constants exported from src/data/migration.ts) has no exploitable issues. No secrets in the diff. Checked threat points: (1) Prototype lookups - every lookup of a task by an id that can come from data (parentTaskId, spawned ids) goes through Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(data.tasks, id) (ES2021-compatible). The only write key is a fresh crypto.randomUUID(), so no prototype-pollution sink. 'constructor'/'__proto__' cases are covered by tests (spawn with parent 'constructor' is a no-op; revert with ['constructor','__proto__'] does not throw and changes nothing). A JSON-parsed '__proto__' key is an own property, so the check handles it correctly. (2) Replacement-pattern injection - formatFollowUpNotice follows tech-spec Decision 7: a single regex /\{(group|count)\}/g with a function replacer, so the group title is inserted literally and never re-scanned. Tests assert that $&, $1, $$, $', $` and {count}/{group} in the title stay literal. (3) Length limits - why is cut to 10 000 before the lone-high-surrogate strip; follow-up text is sliced to 200 before the trailing-anchored regex, so that regex runs on at most 200 chars (no ReDoS surface). The list is capped at 20 before any work per item. The normalization is byte-identical to sanitizeFollowUps, so the next load keeps the saved text unchanged. (4) Surrogate safety - both cuts drop a trailing lone high surrogate; a valid pair ends in a low surrogate and survives; tested. (5) Mutation - spawn/revert mutate the PluginData passed in by design (Decision 3, same as applyStatusTransition). Nothing here reaches data outside the given board and parent (the second-board test confirms this). Whether the store passes a copy is a caller concern for a later task, not a security issue. (6) Isolation - the module imports only types and the two constants from migration.ts; no stores, i18n or obsidian; no import cycle (migration.ts does not import the logic module). 31/31 unit tests pass on Node 22. Out of scope and not flagged: a hand-edited non-object task entry (e.g. "p1": null) is left in `tasks` by taskObjects, so hasTask would pass and pendingFollowUps(null) would throw. This is self-inflicted local data damage that already breaks card rendering before a spawn is reachable, and it is tracked as TD-01 (wider load hardening). Downstream rendering of the notice should keep passing a plain string (Obsidian Notice / text interpolation), never HTML; verify in the task that wires the notice.
